lead: We’re now inside TMD’s 10–14 July rain window, so the North stays on a flash-flood watch through mid-week. Today’s keeper is good news: the government is reviving the domestic tourism co-payment subsidy (up to ฿3,000/head) and weighing visa exemptions for Indian and EU travellers — both aimed at the H2 recovery you’d feel in Chiang Mai. On tech, OpenAI launched GPT-5.6 and “ChatGPT Work”, the clearest sign yet of an off-the-shelf ops copilot for a small hospitality business.

cards.headline: Inside the 10–14 July rain window — the North stays on flash-flood watch through mid-week; Bavi is a non-event for Thailand
cards.summary: What changed: the window TMD flagged is now live rather than forecast. Next 24h — scattered thundershowers with isolated heavy rain across Mae Hong Son, Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai, Phayao, Nan and Uttaradit, with flash-flood and landslide risk near foothills and waterways. Typhoon Bavi is tracking into eastern Fujian, China on 11–12 July, confirmed no direct impact on Thailand. Marine warnings persist: 2–4m waves in the upper Andaman.

wwuw.v: The operational middle of the wet spell, not the start or end. Ground around Chiang Mai stays saturated through mid-week, so flash-flood and landslide risk for guest transfers, airport runs and upcountry excursions carries through at least 14 July. Not an emergency-grade escalation — a “build the buffer into today’s logistics” watch.

Whether TMD or DDPM upgrades the generic 10–14 July language into a formal advisory naming Chiang Mai specifically; Ping River levels as the week’s rain works downstream; and whether the southwest monsoon re-intensifies after Bavi clears.

cards.headline: Two demand levers moving at once: a revived co-payment subsidy (up to ฿3,000/head) plus proposed visa exemptions for Indian and EU travellers
cards.summary: The Tourism & Sports Ministry is drafting a new phase of the state “half-half” co-payment scheme to stimulate H2 travel: ~฿3,000 per person for an initial 1M entitlements, run through the existing Paotang app, bookings expected Q4 2026 (cost split still being set at 50:50 or 60:40; ministry seeking ฿3bn). Alongside it: a proposed 15-day visa exemption for Indian travellers and 30-day for all EU countries, plus ~1M discounted hotel room-nights.

wwuw.v: The demand-side counterweight to a soft China picture. The co-payment scheme historically lifts domestic occupancy in shoulder/low season — directly relevant to Chiang Mai, which leans on Thai weekenders outside the Nov–Feb peak — while an EU/India exemption plays to the long-haul, high-value segment TAT is chasing. If your rooms or packages can list in Paotang, the Q4 booking window is worth planning around now.

Whether the co-payment terms firm up (cost split, per-night cap, eligible property types, whether small operators can enrol via Paotang); the actual effective dates for any India/EU exemption (proposals, not law); and whether the ฿3bn budget request clears.

cards.headline: OpenAI released GPT-5.6 to the public — and “ChatGPT Work,” an agent built to finish whole jobs, not just answer

wwuw.v: On 9 July OpenAI took GPT-5.6 out of preview and made the full three-tier family public — Sol (most capable), Terra (balanced), Luna (fast/cheap) — paired with ChatGPT Work, an agent that gathers context across your apps and files to produce finished documents, spreadsheets, presentations and Codex-style tasks across web, phone and desktop. Altman claims Sol is ~54% more token-efficient on agentic coding; API rates $5/$30 (Sol), $2.50/$15 (Terra), $1/$6 (Luna) per 1M tokens.

The part that matters isn’t the benchmark, it’s ChatGPT Work. An agent that reliably builds a rate sheet, a supplier reconciliation, or a guest-comms doc from your own files is the first mainstream, off-the-shelf version of the “ops copilot” a small hospitality business would actually use — no engineering project required.

“Finishes whole jobs” is the marketing claim; real-world reliability on messy business data is unproven at launch. Connectors, data-handling terms, and Thai-language / mixed-currency handling are open questions. Token efficiency is OpenAI’s own figure.
Independent reviews of ChatGPT Work on real back-office tasks; whether Anthropic/Google ship comparable “agent that ships work” products; and pricing/limits once rollout widens.

podcasts.headline: Neil deGrasse Tyson: aliens, black holes, simulation theory, and why Mars stays uneconomical (9 Jul)
podcasts.summary: A wide-ranging one on the universe’s big mysteries: why geopolitical competition — not curiosity — is what actually funds expensive space missions, why Mars colonisation stays economically impossible without a national incentive, and where AI helps science (replication) versus stalls (genuine innovation). For you: squarely your space/aviation wheelhouse, and the “AI replicates but doesn’t truly innovate” thread is a grounded counterweight to this week’s GPT-5.6 hype.

podcasts.headline: Ep. 840 — Mark Pincus: how to figure out what projects to spend your life on (10 Jul)
podcasts.summary: Zynga founder Mark Pincus on the meta-question behind any venture: how to choose what’s actually worth your time, and how he decides which billion-dollar ideas to chase versus let go. Idea: the hardest founder skill isn’t execution, it’s selection. No Thailand/hospitality angle — a founder-mindset episode, useful if you’re weighing where to point your own time this half.

items.title: Tesla tore down its original Model S/X line in 46 days to build Optimus at Fremont
items.body: Tesla Manufacturing posted footage of the original Model S & X assembly line being decommissioned in just 46 days — “End of an era” — clearing the Fremont floor to scale Optimus Gen 3, with full-scale output expected late July/August. A concrete capacity data point on the humanoid push, not PR fluff. Teslarati

items.title: A silicon chip that “writes” DNA with electricity and enzymes — cleaner synthesis at scale
items.body: Researchers built a silicon chip that writes dozens of DNA sequences simultaneously using electricity and water-based enzymes — a cleaner alternative to chemical DNA synthesis. Faster, parallel, enzyme-driven writing is quiet infrastructure for the whole synthetic-biology and longevity stack — an enabling tool that rarely makes headlines but shows up under a lot of future work. Early-stage lab result. ScienceDaily (materials)

items.title: Some brains fight Alzheimer’s by keeping newborn neurons alive through the damage
items.body: A study found certain brains appear to resist Alzheimer’s by helping immature (newborn) brain cells survive damage instead of dying off — a natural resilience mechanism rather than just plaque-clearing. Mechanism-level, not a therapy, but the kind of “why do some people stay sharp” finding that feeds the healthspan side of longevity research you follow. Peer-reviewed, early. ScienceDaily (healthy aging)

interest.title: Starship Flight 13 is imminent — NET 14–15 July, Booster 20 already on the pad
interest.body: FAA advisories put Starship Flight 13 at No-Earlier-Than 14 July (backup into the 15th), and SpaceX has moved Booster 20 to the pad. Second flight of the all-new V3 stack on Raptor 3, aiming to repeat Flight 12’s suborbital profile — an in-space Raptor relight and a soft ocean splashdown — and prove the revised V3 booster. Space Launch Schedule

interest.title: F1 returns at Spa in 8 days — a wounded Antonelli meets a resurgent Ferrari
interest.body: The championship resumes at the Belgian GP, Spa, 19 July — the last race before the break. Antonelli still leads on 179 pts, +25 over Russell, but he’s finished outside the points in two of the last three rounds, so Spa is a genuine bounce-back test (bookmakers still favour him ~13/8). Ferrari arrives fresh off Leclerc’s Silverstone win. Great drivers’ circuit, often wet. Formula1.com
